title: Volver a: Doing It Again, in Patagonia

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *volver a* + infinitive from B2 Unit 23: it means "do again" and works in every tense (*volvió a llover*, *no volveré a llegar tarde*). In a place of storms and moving ice, many things happen again and again.

sections.title: Volver a in southern Chile
rows: El viento vuelve a soplar con fuerza después de la tormenta.
present: the wind blows hard again
Muchos viajeros vuelven a visitar el parque.
present: many travellers visit the park again
Muchos glaciares no volverán a tener el tamaño de antes.
future with *no*: they will not be the size they were again
El guía no volvió a caminar hasta el glaciar.
past with *no*: the guide did not walk to the glacier again

items.spanish: Después de cada tormenta, el viento vuelve a soplar con fuerza.
items.english: After every storm, the wind blows hard again.

items.spanish: Muchos viajeros que visitan Torres del Paine vuelven a visitarlo.
items.english: Many travellers who visit Torres del Paine visit it again.

items.spanish: Según varios glaciólogos, muchos glaciares no volverán a tener el tamaño de antes.
items.english: According to several glaciologists, many glaciers will not be the size they were before again.

items.spanish: El guía no volvió a caminar hasta el glaciar.
items.english: The guide did not walk to the glacier again.

sections.content: *Volver a* + infinitive is "do again", and *a* cannot be left out. Do not confuse it with *volver a* + place: *Volvió a casa* means "He went back home", not "He did it again".
